correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, exact proof of weight lower bound via dominating pairs and a constructive equality; explicit characterization of all equality cases by active subsets of minimum cycle dominating sets; complete disjoint classification of cyclic gap patterns, with n=3 and n=4 boundaries handled separately; independent full-label checks for n=3..6 plus independent exhaustive core-label checks for n=3..12. No finite extrapolation.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The coefficient of the lowest-degree term in the Italian-domination polynomial is exactly the number of minimum Roman {2}-dominating functions. All these versions were compared; a scalar domination-number formula is not an exact coefficient count.

value.rationale: The exact lowest coefficient of the Italian domination polynomial is a natural graph invariant beyond its scalar domination number. The canonical unicyclic sunlet family lies just beyond the trees and cycles treated by the 2026 counting paper. The residue-one multiplicity arises from an otherwise invisible optional selected label at adjacent length-two gaps. The result is a full structural classification of optimizers for infinitely many graph orders, not an arbitrary tiny finite table; it may inform general unicyclic/corona enumerators.
